_about: Imported from the old GPT project by tools/import_from_gpt.py. Status and feedback are the owner's verdicts; do not upgrade them without the owner's say-so.

conventions.alignment_used_by_gpt: Each frame was scaled uniformly per action, then placed so the head's horizontal centre (median x of the top ~30-38% of opaque pixels) and the lowest opaque pixel line up across frames. Feet were NOT aligned to contact points, which is one suspected cause of sliding.
conventions.facing: right; left-facing versions were made by mirroring

ren.description: Young hooded thief: green hood, brown hair, cream sleeves, dark trousers, boots, brown satchel.

idle.feedback: Accepted as an identity match for the walk. It is one still drawing (GPT repeated it 14 times), so later the owner noted the idle 'does nothing'.

walk_keypose.old_timing: advanced one drawing per 20 game px of travel (= ~41.9 cell px)
walk_keypose.feedback: Liked. Owner wants extra in-between frames for smoothness without losing identity or the poses.

jump.old_timing: 12 fps; position driven by an arc in code
jump.feedback: Positive response in the platform-jump demo. Note the character's look differs from the walk (identity drift) even though it was accepted.

rejected_walk_fourteen.old_timing: one frame per 80/14 game px (= ~12 cell px)
rejected_walk_fourteen.feedback: Owner preferred the 4-pose walk over this. Earlier complaints about generated Ren walks: unstable proportions, too thin, hood/hair/colour changes, uneven motion, sliding.

rejected_walk_flatboy.old_timing: one frame per 8 game px (= ~16.7 cell px)
rejected_walk_flatboy.feedback: Character changed and slid; owner explicitly preferred the 4-pose walk.

unverified_idle_blink.feedback: Never reviewed by the owner. Built with repeated cells.

climb_up.feedback: The grounded ledge climb: after several revisions the owner called it smooth, then 'perfect'. Earlier versions were rejected for reaching into the air and pushing off unsupported positions. Drawn in an older style than the walk, so identity differs.
climb_up.old_scene: Game px, scale 0.4777 (1 game px = 2.093 cell px). Floor y=594. Ledge body x=470..658, top surface y=500 (94 game px = ~197 cell px above the floor); its cap overhangs 8 px each side, so the front edge is x=462. CORRECTED: the path was NOT a straight line. terra_demo/index.html pins Ren's hand per pose over 1.55 s: pose = round(t*13); for poses 1-11 the anchor is placed so the hand pixel hands[pose] (cell px: 1:(395,244) 2:(399,247) 3:(399,247) 4:(402,245) 5:(383,234) 6:(378,231) 7:(388,367) 8:(397,366) 9:(377,420) 10:(371,420) 11:(348,421)) sits at x = 470 + contact[pose] (contact = 0,15,15,15,15,15,20,30,45,60,70,75 game px), with y = floor for poses <= 6 and the hand on the ledge top after that. Pose 0 eases from (425,594) and poses 12-13 ease to (508,500) with smoothstep. annotations/ren/climb_up.json scene.path holds the exact per-frame points. The anchor is the cell's horizontal centre (x=256) and cell y=439.6 (448 - 4/scale).

climb_down.feedback: Pair of the liked grounded climb; used unchanged in the accepted demos.
climb_down.old_scene: Same ledge and the same per-pose hand table as climb_up, run backwards (CORRECTED, not a straight line): played frame k (t=k/13) is positioned by climb_up pose round((1-t)*13) while drawing frame k of this sheet. annotations/ren/climb_down.json scene.path holds the exact per-frame points; the character faces right.

happy.feedback: First-pass reworked sheet (sprite_rework), generated, not individually reviewed. The owner found the rework promising overall but flagged identity drift between Ren's actions.

interact.feedback: First-pass rework: crouches, reaches the ground, stands (a pickup). The old demo removed the apple during the hand-down part at 0.58 s; the hand was not attached to the item. Not individually reviewed.

hurt_stumble.feedback: First-pass rework: loses balance and recovers. Not individually reviewed.

caught_game_over.feedback: First-pass rework: surprise to sitting, for being caught. Not individually reviewed.

look_around.feedback: First-pass rework: glances up and returns. Not individually reviewed.

ladder_up.feedback: First-pass rework, rear view. GPT's ladder down was this reversed. Hand/foot contact with rungs never checked.

guard.description: Grumpy mustached guard: silver armour and helmet, blue sash/tabard, brown belt and gloves, sheathed sword.

idle.feedback: Much too fast. Analysis suggests only ~3-4 distinct drawings.

walk.feedback: Same problem as idle. Frames repeat similar steps; no clear passing pose; first priority to diagnose.

ladder_up.feedback: Bad. Ladder down was this sequence reversed; also bad.

climb_up.feedback: Owner could not judge without a ledge to see contact. Frame 08 was swapped for an earlier pose because the generated one was cropped.

climb_down.feedback: Owner could not judge without a ledge.

reference.reference/ren_identity_drift_example.png: Side-by-side of Ren's old actions showing costume, proportion, face and colour changes between actions; the kind of drift the tools should catch.
